ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to engagement, every shareholder, director, UBO, and authorized signatory must be screened against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) lists and domestic terrorist financing lists, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN list due to USD wire clearing via United States correspondent banks, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and the UK HM Treasury sanctions list. Continuous monitoring is required for at least 180 days after onboarding. Each screened person must be checked for PEP status, state-owned enterprise affiliation, adverse media, politically exposed family members, and negative regulatory history. Any PEP hit, OFAC or UN match, or source-of-funds anomaly triggers enhanced due diligence, written source-of-wealth evidence, and senior management approval before Korean incorporation proceeds. All screening results must be retained for the statutory AML record-keeping period.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry Office (iROS) at www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered trade name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be expressed in Hangul as the authoritative legal name. English or Latin-script names may be used only as supplementary transliterations and cannot be the sole registered name. The statutory four-tier naming doctrine requires: first, a distinctive Hangul trade name; second, a Hangul transliteration of the English legal name Yuhan Hoesa; third, a Hangul statement of the specific business purpose (long-haul bonded highway freight transport under TIR Carnets); and fourth, a mandatory legal entity suffix denoting limited liability, i.e., Yuhan Hoesa or Jusik Hoesa. Chinese characters are not recognized as a substitute for Hangul and cannot independently satisfy the registered-name requirement.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 calendar days of the registration court written rejection, the applicant may submit a written objection to the court registry through iROS or in person, attaching the name-search certificate, the proposed Hangul name, the ISIC 5221 business-purpose statement, and legal grounds under Articles 18 through 22 of the Commercial Act. The registry manager must issue a written disposition. If the objection is denied, the applicant may file an immediate appeal to the competent District Court under the Non-Contentious Civil Litigation Procedure Act within 14 days after receipt of the denial. The name reservation does not automatically extend during appeal, so the applicant should concurrently file a fresh name-search request and, if possible, seek pre-clearance with the commercial registration officer before final re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox-only address is not recommended for this industry. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, the Korea Customs Service, and the National Tax Service (NTS) will generally reject a TIR Carnet carrier license unless the registered office is a fixed physical location in the Republic of Korea where management records, vehicle maintenance files, driver employment documents, customs paperwork, and tax records are kept. Korean banks will also reject a virtual address for corporate account opening in the long-haul bonded trucking sector because fuel-card clearing, vehicle registration, and SWIFT wire documentation require physical presence and periodic due-diligence visits. A fully serviced physical suite with exclusive filing space, a visible nameplate, and a designated local manager is the minimum acceptable commercial-substance arrangement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified inspection risk: approximately 20% within the first 6 months after incorporation and 40% within the first 24 months after obtaining the TIR transport license. The probability rises to 65% if three or more of the following triggers are present: NTS address mismatch, zero declared employees at the registered office, a month-to-month virtual office lease, any P.O. Box mailing address, abnormal fuel-card or bank cash-flow patterns, customs declaration volume inconsistent with office capacity, absence of a physical nameplate, or closure of the office during municipal business hours. Mitigation checklist: lease a physical office, display the nameplate, keep original invoices and TIR/Carnet records on site, employ at least one local administrative person, maintain payroll records, and respond to all NTS and registry correspondence within the legal deadline.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as most recently amended), Articles 287 through 319; Commercial Registration Act, Article 34; Trucking Transport Business Act, Articles 3 and 5; Customs Convention on the International Transport of Goods under Cover of TIR Carnets
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Section, District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; in Seoul, Seoul Central District Court Registry Office; online portal: Internet Registration Office of the Korean Court Administration
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Korean Commercial Act for a Yuhan Hoesa; no blocked escrow account is required. However, the full subscribed capital must be deposited in a designated domestic bank account before registration and evidenced by a capital deposit certificate. For the international trucking licence, MOLIT may assess financial solvency and TIR carnet issuance may require a bank guarantee from the national guaranteeing association.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF KR_YUHANGHOESA (YUHAN HOESA / LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY). RESOLVED: (1) That the Board has reviewed the Korean Commercial Act, the notarized Articles of Incorporation of the Company, and the certificate of registration of the Company, and confirms that the Company has been validly incorporated and duly registered with the competent court registry. (2) That the authorized capital of the Company is [●] Korean Won, divided into [●] contributions with a stated value of [●] Korean Won each, and that each contribution has been fully subscribed and paid by the respective member as recorded in the membership register, with no unpaid contribution liability outstanding. (3) That the registered office of the Company is established at [●], Republic of Korea, and the Managing Director is hereby authorized to execute, sign, and deliver the lease agreement, utility contracts, and all associated documents necessary to maintain the registered office and to notify all relevant government agencies of the registered address. (4) That the Company shall open, operate, and maintain corporate bank accounts at [●] Bank, including a general corporate account, a fuel-card clearing account, and a SWIFT wire transfer account, and that the Managing Director together with one additional authorized signatory designated by the Board shall have authority to execute banking mandates, currency control declarations, anti-money laundering forms, and payment instructions. (5) That [●] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and Representative Director of the Company with full power to act in all corporate, regulatory, and contractual matters; [●] is appointed Director and Company Secretary; and [●] is appointed Auditor to the extent required by law, each to hold office until the next annual members meeting and until successors are duly elected. (6) That the Managing Director is authorized to apply for and obtain the business registration certificate, the international cargo trucking transport business licence, TIR carnet holder registration, customs brokerage arrangements, and any other operating permits necessary for long-haul bonded highway freight transport. (7) That all banking and legal authorities be evidenced by certified copies of this resolution and by a certificate of incumbency issued by the Company Secretary. (8) That this resolution may be signed in counterparts and is effective from the date of incorporation registration; all prior resolutions inconsistent with this resolution are hereby superseded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve corporate name and prepare notarized articles of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internet Registration Office of the Korean Court Administration and the Commercial Registration Section of the District Court with jurisdiction over the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators or their duly authorized legal representative must access the court e-registration portal or attend the commercial registry office. A name search must be conducted to ensure the proposed corporate name is available and does not conflict with a previously registered company. The draft Articles of Incorporation must be prepared in Korean, with an English translation for the corporate record, setting forth the corporate name, business purpose, registered office location, total subscribed capital, valuation of non-cash contributions if any, number of members, and the names and resident registration numbers of directors and auditor. The business purpose clause must expressly include long-haul bonded highway freight transport and TIR carnets operations. The draft is then circulated for notarization after legal review by a licensed Korean attorney.
required_dossiers: Corporate name search report
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Passport or national identity card of each incorporator
Power of attorney if signed by a representative
Proof of address of the proposed registered office
English translation of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects or queries the name due to similarity with an existing entity, the applicant must reserve a new name or obtain a written consent or non-conflict letter from the prior registered company and refile the name reservation within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit subscribed capital in a domestic custodial bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A designated domestic commercial bank in Korea, such as the bank selected by the incorporators in the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators must open a dedicated temporary capital subscription account in the name of the company under incorporation and deposit the full amount of the subscribed capital contribution. Each member must make the contribution in cash or, if approved, in kind with a statutory valuation certificate. Since Korean law imposes no minimum paid-in capital for a Yuhan Hoesa, the amount contributed should nevertheless be sufficient to satisfy the financial soundness standards applied by MOLIT for an international cargo trucking licence and by the TIR guaranteeing association. The bank will issue a capital deposit certificate, which is an essential registration annex. Foreign source remittances must be reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and subjected to the bank's customer due diligence and anti-money laundering review.
required_dossiers: Application for temporary capital deposit account
Identification documents of all members
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Source of funds declaration
Foreign exchange transaction report if capital is remitted from abroad
Bank capital deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, the applicant must provide certified source-of-wealth evidence such as bank statements, tax records, or a legal opinion. If the bank refuses the account, the incorporators may select another licensed Korean bank and transfer the deposit before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarize the articles of incorporation before a Korean notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed Korean notary public affiliated with the Korea Notary Association, typically located in Seoul or the city where the registered office will be established
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All incorporators must appear in person before the notary or be represented by an attorney-in-fact holding a duly notarized and apostilled power of attorney. The notary verifies the identity of each incorporator, confirms the legal capacity of the parties, reviews the Articles of Incorporation for compliance with the Korean Commercial Act, and certifies the signatures and the establishment of the company as a Yuhan Hoesa. The notarial certificate must be attached to the final Articles of Incorporation. If the notary finds a mandatory provision missing or defective, the articles must be amended, re-signed, and re-notarized before proceeding to court registration. Notarization is a strict precondition to the submission of the incorporation application to the court registry.
required_dossiers: Original Articles of Incorporation for notarization
Capital deposit certificate
Identity documents of each incorporator
Power of attorney and notarized ID of the attorney-in-fact, if applicable
Consent forms of appointed directors and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses certification because of a defective or missing clause, the incorporators must correct the Articles of Incorporation, convene all members for signature, and pay a new notary fee if a fresh notarial procedure is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Yuhan Hoesa with the competent District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Section of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The representative director or authorized agent must submit the completed Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital deposit certificate, consent letters of directors and auditor, and proof of payment of registration tax, education surtax, and court filing fees. The court examiner verifies the statutory requirements, including the lawfulness of the corporate purpose, the accuracy of the capital contribution, and the validity of the officers. If all documents are in order, the registry enters the company onto the commercial register and issues a certificate of registered matters, which is the definitive proof of the company's legal existence. Electronic filing through the Internet Registration Office is accepted and may reduce physical attendance requirements.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate
Consent to appointment of directors and auditor
Certificate of payment of registration tax and court fees
Identification and resident registration proofs of directors
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court registry issues a supplementary order, the applicant must cure the specified defects within the mandated correction period, usually two weeks, by submitting the corrected document or a written explanation. If the application is rejected, the applicant may petition the competent court for review or file a new complete application after curing the defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain tax, trucking, and TIR operating authorizations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service; Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport regional licensing office; Korea Customs Service and the national guaranteeing association for TIR carnets
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the certificate of registered matters is obtained, the company must register for corporate income tax and value-added tax and obtain a business registration certificate from the competent district tax office. For the international cargo trucking business, the company must file a trucking transport business licence application with the MOLIT regional office, providing evidence of ownership or long-term lease of compliant articulated vehicles, secure parking or depot facilities, mandatory liability insurance, and financial capacity. The company must also apply to the Korea Customs Service through the Korean TIR guaranteeing association for approval as a TIR carnet holder, and execute the TIR guarantee undertaking. Customs may inspect the vehicle fleet, record-keeping systems, and operational premises before final authorization.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registered matters from the court registry
Business registration application and corporate registration certificate
Trucking transport business licence application
MOLIT compliance form for vehicle parking and depot facilities
Vehicle registration certificates and inspection records
Commercial liability and cargo insurance certificates
Financial solvency evidence including bank balances
TIR carnet holder application and guarantee undertaking
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOLIT suspends or denies the trucking licence for inadequate financial capacity, the company may submit a bank guarantee, corporate parent guarantee, or capital increase certificate. If Korea Customs Service rejects the TIR holder application, the company may correct any customs compliance deficiency, reapply through a licensed customs broker, or administratively appeal under the Customs Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT), International Trucking Business Licensing Division; Korea Customs Service (KCS), TIR Carnet Authorization Office; National Fire Agency and local municipal fire departments for depot and fuel storage permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: International Cargo Trucking Transport Business Licence under the Trucking Transport Business Act and TIR Carnet Holder Authorisation under the Customs Convention on the International Transport of Goods under Cover of TIR Carnets

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MOE), Environmental Impact Assessment Support Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for pure mobile cross-border TIR trucking operations. If the company establishes a fixed bonded cargo terminal, truck depot, or workshop with floor area exceeding 10,000 square meters, it falls under Environmental Registration (Category C) under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act; a full Environmental Impact Assessment report is required only for terminals exceeding 100,000 square meters or located in environmentally sensitive zones.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For pure trucking there is no stationary industrial discharge. For any fixed depot, wastewater discharged to public waters must comply with the Water Environment Conservation Act effluent standards, including BOD not more than 40 mg/L, TOC not more than 40 mg/L, TSS not more than 40 mg/L, and pH between 5.8 and 8.6, or with the receiving municipal sewer standards. Fuel storage tanks must comply with the Clean Air Conservation Act VOC emission controls, including vapor recovery on gasoline or diesel loading lines and a total non-methane volatile organic compound concentration generally capped at 200 ppm at storage tank vents. Hazardous waste from vehicle maintenance must be stored in labeled containers and transported only by licensed hazardous waste carriers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Operation Certificate from the National Fire Agency or local fire station is required for any truck depot, parking building, maintenance workshop, or office; dangerous goods storage permits are required for diesel fuel storage above regulatory thresholds under the Dangerous Substances Safety Act. Fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and evacuation plans must be certified for all physical premises. The Ministry of Employment and Labor must issue or receive a workplace safety and health inspection approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including structural load review for any mezzanine, racking, or elevated maintenance platform, and all trucks must carry vehicle inspection certificates and fire suppression equipment compliant with Korea road transport safety regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online portal: HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr). Export/customs clearance authority: Korea Customs Service (KCS) via the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. The Yuhan Hoesa is formed as a domestic Korean limited liability company and must be registered with the competent district tax office, not as a foreign non-resident branch. 2. Within 20 days of commencing business, file the prescribed Business Registration Application with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the head office or place of business; if no domestic place of business exists, register through a statutorily appointed Korean tax representative. 3. Attach the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, the foreign parent/shareholder's registration certificate and TIN, authenticated proxy in favor of the Korean tax representative, proof of the registered domestic address or business facility, the transport license and TIR operating authorization evidence, and the contract evidencing commencement of cross-border trucking activity. 4. The NTS will issue the Business Registration Certificate and assign the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which is the unified TIN/VAT registration number used for corporate income tax, VAT, withholding tax, and customs purposes. 5. Separately, the entity must enroll as a bonded transporter/exporter in the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system and include the TIR carnet guarantee/issuing association details in the customs registration file. 6. Any subsequent change in foreign controller, Korean tax representative, address, or TIR operating scope must be reported to the NTS and KCS within the statutory update windows.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not operate an IRS-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election regime for domestic Yuhan Hoesa LLCs. A foreign investor may choose between a domestic Korean corporation and a foreign corporation branch, but once formed as a domestic Yuhan Hoesa, entity-level corporate income tax and VAT classification are compulsory; no pass-through or territorial election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea, administered by the National Tax Service
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for a corporation. VAT registration is triggered by business commencement; a Yuhan Hoesa must register within 20 days of starting business. The KRW 80,000,000 simplified taxable person annual turnover threshold applies only to eligible individual entrepreneurs and does not exempt corporate taxpayers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The Republic of Korea operates an electronic tax invoice (e-Tax invoice) transmission regime through HomeTax; there is no real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory anti-fraud digital stamping engine in Korea. A VAT-registered supplier must issue an e-Tax invoice through HomeTax or an NTS-approved electronic invoicing service provider and transmit it to the NTS by the statutory filing deadline; semi-annual VAT returns then reconcile all e-invoices. For zero-rated TIR exports, the e-Tax invoice must state the zero-rated export nature, and the KCS UNI-PASS export declaration data is cross-checked with NTS HomeTax records. Computerized issuers using bulk, API, or EDI transmission must register their e-invoicing systems with the NTS; the NTS performs post-filing cross-matching and audit rather than real-time fiscal approval.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for the TIR overland trucking supply is available under the Korean VAT Act where the factual and documentary evidence establishes that: (a) goods were physically exported from the Republic of Korea through a Korean customs office under an accepted Export Customs Declaration; (b) the transport service is performed by the Korean Yuhan Hoesa as part of the international carriage of those goods, or is supplied to a foreign customer as a foreign-currency-earning service qualifying for zero-rating; (c) the TIR Carnet traverses the Korean border under customs seal and is discharged at the foreign destination; and (d) the freight consideration is received and repatriated in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Domestic Korean road haulage that does not leave Korean territory is taxable at 10% unless a specific statutory zero-rating provision applies; the Korean non-sealed domestic leg of an international movement is also taxable at 10% unless adequately evidenced as an international freight service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Customs Declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS (Export Declaration Certificate and electronic control number)
TIR Carnet with the Korean customs departure-office certificate, green cover, and foreign customs discharge receipt evidencing that the goods exited Korea and arrived abroad
CMR international waybill (Convention on the Contract for the International Carriage of Goods by Road) with matching consignor/consignee, goods description, weight, route, and truck registration
Commercial invoice, packing list, freight contract, and export sales/purchase documents reconciled to the Export Customs Declaration

Foreign exchange collection certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank (inward remittance certificate, being the Korean statutory equivalent to an FIRC) evidencing receipt of the export freight consideration
Where applicable, a multimodal transport document, such as a combined transport bill of lading or ocean/air waybill, for the onward sea or air leg after the Korean road section
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and KCS jointly audit zero-rated TIR exports by matching the UNI-PASS export exit record, the HomeTax e-Tax invoice, the TIR/CMR transport trail, and the foreign exchange collection certificate. If any mandatory document is missing or inconsistent, the NTS will retroactively disallow the 0% rate, assess 10% VAT on the freight consideration, disallow input VAT credits attributable to the supply, add late-payment surcharges, and impose underreporting penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes, including up to 40% for dishonest underreporting or evasion and lesser percentages for negligent reporting. Fraudulent use of TIR carnets, false customs declarations, or forged export documents may also be prosecuted under the Customs Act and the Punishment of Tax Crimes Act, exposing the entity and responsible officers to criminal fines, imprisonment, and retrospective reassessment within the statutory limitation period for tax fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIN) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a fundamentally liberalised foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with the Korean won (KRW) fully convertible for current account transactions including trade in goods, transportation, travel, and routine service fees. Capital account transactions, such as cross-border equity injections into a Korean LLC (Yuhan Hoesa), are permitted but subject to the outward/inward reporting regime administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Bank of Korea. Foreign investments exceeding a certain threshold require declaration under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act with a Korea Trade Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or designated foreign exchange bank report. There are no mandatory surrender requirements for export proceeds; a South Korean resident entity may hold foreign currency receipts in domestic foreign currency accounts for up to 18 months without compulsory conversion. Profit remittance from the LLC to non-resident shareholders is treated as current account payment and is freely convertible once a certified tax clearance and audited financial statement confirm the distributable reserves. However, practical friction arises from banks requiring statutory documents, tax completion certificates, and the foreign investor's proof of original foreign exchange transaction certificates to prevent disguised capital flight. Overall, Korea is a low-intervention jurisdiction with no parallel market premium, but the administrative reporting framework creates a compliance burden for any entity lacking robust treasury support.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 12 and Enforcement Decree 7-2 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be collected or received within 18 months from the date of export customs clearance (the standard settlement period). Extensions are available upon application to the relevant foreign exchange bank if justifiable circumstances exist. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; the exporting entity may retain 100% of foreign currency earnings in a foreign currency account, but quarterly outstanding export proceeds must be reported to the designated foreign exchange bank to ensure compliance with the collection timeline and to facilitate the bank's monitoring of trade financing exposure.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (USD/KRW multi-currency) with Foreign Exchange Bank designation
Capital Escrow Account for FDI declaration and operating current account
Trade Settlement Account with TIR-related documentary collection and LC facilities
Secondary Foreign Currency Settlement Account for Export Proceeds

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI (Electronic Money Institution) and non-bank virtual account services have very low feasibility for a Korean-regulated Yuhan Hoesa in the trucking/logistics sector. The FETA and the Korean Banking Act strictly require that all foreign exchange transactions undertaken by a domestic resident entity be executed through a domestic designated foreign exchange bank with a real local branch presence. Offshore EMI platforms cannot obtain a licensed foreign exchange bank status in Korea for the purpose of holding trade proceeds or effecting KRW settlements. They lack access to the FEIN reporting system, which mandates that every foreign exchange transaction be reported on a real-time basis. Fintechs such as Wise or Revolut Business have no legal standing to provide KRW IBANs or local clearing accounts for a Korean LLC and would breach the Korean Government's Foreign Exchange Information Network requirements. Their viability is therefore rated 'Not Viable'; the treasurer must rely exclusively on Tier-1 domestic bank channels for all FX and clearing operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean banking regulators and internal AML policies of Tier-1 commercial banks mandate a physical appearance of the statutory directors and the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) for the initial corporate account opening. Remote opening is not generally permissible for a foreign-owned LLC without a local representative physically present in the branch. However, if an authorised local representative has been appointed via a notarised and apostilled power of attorney, some banks permit the UBOs to complete interviews through a two-way video call from a consulate, provided that the consulate attests identity. Yet majority of Tier-1 banks, especially Shinhan and Kookmin, insist that at least one statutory director or the authorised local representative physically attends the 'face-to-face KYC' interview to sign the EUC, Section 244(b) declarations, and Foreign Exchange Bank confirmations. Failure to do so triggers a hard rejection. Legalising the corporate book with a Hague Apostille and providing certified translations of all statutory documents are mandatory prerequisites.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO and statutory director with a complex ownership chain and no visible in-country economic substance in the trucking sector.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a comprehensive corporate ownership tree up to the ultimate individual shareholder, audited financial statements of the parent (if any), a certified Korean translation of the Articles of Incorporation, notarised passports and proof of address of all UBOs, apostilled power of attorney, and a formal business plan demonstrating the Korean premises, operational fleet, and planned employment contracts. A lease agreement for a physical logistics office and a commitment letter for hiring local staff significantly reduce the 'shell entity' suspicion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained large early-stage capital injection expected from abroad for a newly formed LLC without a clear track record in long-haul bonded trucking.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the source of funds proven by 12 months of audited bank statements from the sending corporate entity, signed share subscription agreements, the foreign exchange bank confirmation of the inward remittance under the designated trade or FDI purpose code (e.g., '109' for foreign direct investment equity), and a projected cash flow model showing how the capital will be deployed for TIR carnet deposits, fleet acquisition, and cross-border fuel card collateral. Include a sworn affidavit that funds do not originate from sanctions-prohibited sources.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade activity in bonded trucking under TIR riska with a high volume of cash-intensive fuel payments and frequent cross-border settlements that may be perceived as money laundering channels.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the TIR Carnet registration certificate, the Korean Customs Service transaction records for the past 1-2 years, copies of issued CMR waybills, GPS fleet tracking logs, and the loading/unloading signed confirmations from bonded terminals. Additionally, provide a fuel-card settlement report from a licensed fuel card issuer that traces every fuelling transaction to a specific vehicle, along with independent third-party accounting verification of the trade cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential on-negative-news screening or sanctions red-flags triggered by a payment counterparty located in a high-risk logistics corridor or shared truck stop jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Publish a detailed counterparty due diligence file containing sanctions screening snapshots from the UN, EU, OFAC, and Korean Financial Intelligence Unit lists for every significant consignee, shipper, and logistics partner. Provide the signed contractual clauses specifying no terrorism, drug trafficking, or sanctions evasion activities, and commit to a quarterly negative-news surveillance report. For any counterparty with a name-match issue, supply the UBO identification, adverse-media review memo, and the corporate officer's sworn reliance letter.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For an inbound foreign direct investment into the Korean LLC, the non-resident shareholder shall remit funds via the SWIFT MT103 message through a correspondent bank to the Shinhan Bank or KB Kookmin capital escrow account. The remittance instruction must include the Korean foreign investment declaration number issued by the MOEF/KOTRA and the standard purpose code 'FDI_EQ' or '109' (equity participation). The receiving designated foreign exchange bank verifies the declaration, credits the escrow account, and later reclasses the funds as paid-in capital upon submission of the certified capital subscription agreement and the certificate of foreign currency purchase. For trade-context inbound payments (e.g., freight receivable for a TIR transport), the routing must use the current account purpose code '10-2-03-01' (transportation earnings) and be supported by the corresponding CMR and TIR Carnet. The bank follows the Foreign Exchange Information Network protocol and releases funds to the operating KRW current account. A capital verification deed is required if the LLC is required to undergo statutory auditing or needs to prove capitalisation for tendering contracts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury operations for the Yuhan Hoesa are cleared through a combination of the designated Tier-1 bank's trade portal, SWIFT MT103 for high-value freight refuelling and cargo insurance payments, and documentary channels. For international TIR trucking operating costs such as diesel, tolls, and third-party logistics subcontractors, the company should use MT103 wires with the purpose code '10-2-01' (trade-related service payments) and attach the underlying purchase orders and service invoices to avoid quarantine under South Korea's name-matching risk filters. For large bonded cargo purchases where the firm acts as a purchasing intermediary, the treasury should open an Irrevocable Documentary Credit (Letter of Credit) against the CMR transport documents and original customs forms; the LC fits the standard UCP600 framework. For lower-risk and time-flexible inventory acquisitions from trucking parts suppliers, an Export/Import Documentary Collection (D/P and D/A) is permissible, though slower, and provides a clean evidence trail required by the Korean Customs Service for the TIR Carnet closure. All outbound payments beyond KRW equivalent of USD 50,000 require a basic declaration to the foreign exchange bank; payments above USD 500,000 require prior submission of a trade contract and, in certain grater risk situations, bank approval from the Ministry of Economy and Finance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Korea Won / USD Deliverable Forward Contracts under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for commercial hedging of cross-border trucking receivables or payables with a firm export/import underlying trade; must be executed through a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank with no speculative position exceeding 3 months of actual exposure.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): permitted for non-resident counterparties or for entities that cannot verify a legitimate current-account exposure; Korean resident companies may enter NDFs only for the purpose of hedging export/import proceeds, and the notional must be capped at the outstanding trade receivable/paid amount with a maturity aligned to the underlying TIR payment cycle.

Currency Swaps (cross-currency settlements) used for synthetic hedging of long-term debt funding from a non-resident parent, subject to MOEF reporting; the company must demonstrate that the swap is designed to reduce interest rate and FX risk on a recognised foreign currency facility, and the swap must be collateralised through the domestic Tier-1 bank's internal treasury desk.

Over-The-Counter Currency Options (EUR/USD or KRW/USD) from the designated bank, only for commercial hedge purposes and constrained by the total net exposed position derived from the TIR freight invoices and fuel card settlements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting Minutes and Resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: N/A - internal corporate governance requirement under the Korean Commercial Act; no regulatory filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (for calendar-year entity: by March 31 of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the ordinary general meeting may expose directors to criminal fines or civil damages under the Commercial Act; repeated non-compliance may be treated as grounds for court-ordered dissolution, but no direct administrative strike-off is triggered

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year (for calendar-year entity: by March 31 of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 2,000,000 under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; loss of tax and FX facilitation benefits; repeated failures may prompt review of foreign investment status but do not directly cause automatic strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (for calendar-year entity: by March 31 of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 10% of unpaid corporate tax for negligent underreporting, 20% for fraudulent underreporting; late-payment interest of 0.022% per day; persistent non-payment leads to forced collection, asset seizure, and possible court-ordered dissolution; no administrative strike-off exists solely for tax delinquency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax on Corporate Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as corporate income tax return, within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (for calendar-year entity: by March 31 of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local surtax penalties mirror national corporate tax penalties: 10% additional tax for underreporting, 20% for fraudulent omission, plus daily late-payment interest; persistent delinquency may result in forced seizure of local assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Quarterly Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Four quarterly filings per calendar year: 1st quarter by April 25, 2nd quarter by July 25, 3rd quarter by October 25, 4th quarter by January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 10% on unpaid VAT, up to 20% if no return is filed; daily late-payment interest of 0.03%; persistent non-filing can lead to seizure of business assets and administrative closure of the business place

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (attached to corporate income tax return) and presented to shareholders before the ordinary general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the ordinary general meeting and by the corporate income tax filing deadline (for calendar-year entity: by March 31 of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If mandatory external audit is omitted, penalties under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies apply: fines up to KRW 50,000,000 for executives, criminal sanctions for wilful omission, and severe impairment of credit plus regulatory disqualification

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% progressive top rate (9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on taxable income from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 24% on taxable income exceeding KRW 20 billion), plus 10% local income tax surtax on the national corporate income tax
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Effective top corporate burden is approximately 26.4% when the local income tax surtax is included. Tax incentives include 100% corporate income tax exemption in designated foreign investment zones for the first 5 years and 50% exemption for the following 2 years; R&D tax credits ranging from 10% to 40%; job-creation and employment-support credits; tax support for bonded logistics and free trade zone operators; accelerated depreciation for environmentally protective equipment. No general patent box is available, but qualifying technology-transfer income can benefit from partial reductions under the Special Taxation Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (main form with annexed Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing system (www.hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing for each fiscal year; interim tax return for the first six months of the fiscal year is due within two months after that six-month period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the statutory deadline is 31 March, extendable to 30 April when the return is prepared by a licensed tax agent and filed electronically.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resident or non-resident entity classification and place of effective management declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark the Yuhan Hoesa as a domestic corporation if its head office or place of effective management is in Korea. Korean incorporation alone makes the entity a domestic corporation; non-resident shareholders controlling management abroad does not automatically override Korean taxation without OECD POEM analysis. Attach board minutes, dispatch logs, driver employment records, and border operation evidence if challenged.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross freight revenue, fuel surcharges, tolls, TIR facilitation charges, and foreign branch turnover.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all Korean-source and internationally allocated trucking revenue attributable to the Korean PE. For TIR cross-border transit, document consignor and consignee locations, customs office records, and contract negotiation points to support source-country allocation; unsupported routing may be reclassified as Korean-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating costs, including driver wages, fuel card clearing, vehicle leasing, depot rent, maintenance, insurance, TIR guarantee premiums, and intercompany service charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All intercompany fuel card, logistics, route management, and TIR guarantee fees must be at arm's length and evidenced by invoices, bank transfers, and Core Income-Generating Activities documents. Payments to non-resident related parties that cannot be substantiated are disallowed and can be reclassified as constructive dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International related-party transaction schedule and transfer pricing adjustment line.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the entity triggers the statutory threshold, attach the Local File, Master File, or Country-by-Country Report. Use a defensible transactional net margin method for cross-border trucking, and show that dispatcher control, route planning, and fuel procurement are economically real. Failure to file or deliberate omission exposes the corporation to reallocation and penalties of 10% to 20% of the understated tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss carryforward, deductions, tax credits, and final national corporate income tax and local income tax calculation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim foreign dividends, royalties, or non-resident management fees as deductible expenses. Claim foreign tax credits only with valid tax residency certificates and source-country corroboration; report whether withholding was applied at 22% or at the applicable DTA reduced rate. Interest-free or low-interest loans from non-residents can trigger deemed dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident profit distributions, withholding tax reconciliation, and treaty relief schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before remitting dividends to non-resident shareholders, deposit the 22% withholding tax unless the recipient has obtained an approved treaty reduction; attach the Application for Exemption or Reduction of Withholding Tax and beneficial ownership declaration. The omission of this attachment in a cross-border distribution is a fatal audit red flag and may impose personal director liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a statutory non-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax, or 10% when the return is filed but tax is understated; a late-payment surcharge accrues at approximately 0.022% per day. Fraudulent evasion is additionally punishable under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act Article 3 by imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to KRW 200 million, plus collection disposition, asset seizure, and travel restriction.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax; treaty-exempt or treaty-reduced rates apply only after formal DTA approval).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident payee must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from its residence country tax authority and submit it to the Korean payer. The Korean payer must file an Application for Exemption or Reduction of Withholding Tax under the relevant DTA before payment, or the payee must file a refund claim with the National Tax Service within 3 years. Beneficial ownership must be proven by board resolutions, bank records, evidence of substantial business activity outside Korea, and no back-to-back conduit arrangements; treaty benefits are denied where the Principal Purpose Test fails or the foreign entity lacks economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding is 22% for both cross-border royalties and interest. Treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 0-15% and royalties to 5-15%, depending on the specific DTA and whether the recipient is the beneficial owner, is a bank, or satisfies the limitation-on-benefits provisions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File preparation is triggered when cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion; Master File preparation is triggered when Korean revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion; Country-by-Country Reporting is required for MNE groups with consolidated revenue above the OECD threshold as implemented by Korea, currently approximately KRW 1 trillion for ultimate parent groups.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations, but it applies a strict substance-over-form doctrine, the National Tax Basic Act Article 14, the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test, and the Framework Act on International Tax Adjustment Articles 3 and 6. The Yuhan Hoesa must demonstrate that Core Income-Generating Activities for cross-border TIR trucking are performed in Korea: board and management decisions, driver employment, fleet ownership or true leasing, fuel procurement, maintenance, insurance placement, freight billing, and TIR carnet control. If management fee payments are made to a foreign principal while substantive transport operations remain in Korea, profits will be reattributed to the Korean PE and treaty relief will be denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Billing Korean and international TIR freight through a nominee intermediary in a low-tax jurisdiction while Korean drivers, dispatchers, fuel purchases, maintenance decisions, and TIR carnet documents are controlled by the Korean Yuhan Hoesa directors, and filing a zero or understated Korean corporate tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment under the Corporate Tax Act, a 10-20% negligence penalty, and a 0.022% per-day late-payment surcharge. Fraudulent evasion is punishable under Punishment of Tax Evasion Act Article 3 with imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to KRW 200 million, plus asset seizure and collection of unpaid corporate tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced under Korean Commercial Act Article 401; directors are jointly and severally liable for tortious losses caused by intentional or negligent management. National Tax Service may blacklist the directors, impose travel bans, attach personal bank accounts, collect the corporate tax from personal assets, and recommend criminal indictment. A court can impose imprisonment on the directors who signed the false return.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation / Inflated Intercompany Deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive management, route-intangible, fuel-card, and logistics service fees to a foreign related party solely to erode the Korean taxable base; setting the Korean operating margin near zero while the offshore related party retains disproportionate profit; failing to prepare the mandatory Local File, Master File, or international transaction schedule.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Framework Act on International Tax Adjustment Articles 2 and 4 authorizes the National Tax Service to adjust to the arm's-length price and to make correlative adjustments; understated tax is assessed with a penalty of up to 20%, plus daily late-payment surcharge and, in flagrant cases, criminal referral for tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign intercompany agreements without commercial substance and without functional and risk analysis are personally exposed under Korean Commercial Act Article 401. The National Tax Service can pierce the corporate form, attach personal property, deny foreign travel, blacklist the directors, and impose imprisonment of up to 3 years where false or incomplete information is submitted knowingly.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Failure / Shell Shareholder Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring and remitting dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resident without withholding the 22% statutory tax, or using a paper-company shareholder in a treaty jurisdiction that has no beneficial ownership, no employees, no activity, and no ability to manage the distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Corporate Tax Act Article 98 makes the Korean payer liable for the un-withheld amount, plus an additional 10% non-compliance penalty and daily late-payment surcharge. The Framework Act on International Tax Adjustment anti-abuse rules and the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act Article 3 apply where the arrangement is fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable if the corporation transfers funds abroad and cannot satisfy the withholding liability. Under Korean Commercial Act Article 401 and the tax collection framework, the National Tax Service may pierce the corporate veil, impose personal assessment, asset freeze, foreign-travel blacklisting, restitution orders, and criminal fines; imprisonment of up to 3 years may follow for deliberate failure to withhold and remit.
